subject: Privacy: vendor flagging, notification cadence and objection runbook
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-12T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Vendor notification: upcoming subprocessor additions and proposed objection cadence

Hi Liam —

Per our onboarding checklist for the integration, attached is our current subprocessor inventory (subprocessor_inventory_20261112.csv). There are three new processors we plan to add that may handle EU customer data. Before we publish the change to your tenant, we want to confirm notification and objection timing so both sides have a clear runbook.

Proposed approach:
- Notification: 30 days prior to activation (email + portal notification)
- Objection window: 30 days from first notification; if an objection is raised, escalate to a joint risk call within 7 business days
- Final decision: if unresolved after 15 days from escalation, fall back to SCCs + documented compensating controls while we remediate

Action items I need from you:
1) Confirm AcmeCloud can accept e-signature execution (DocuSign or AdobeSign) for the DPA amendment and whether you have a preferred envelope flow
2) Confirm whether a 30-day quiet/objection window works, or if you require 45 days given your internal procurement cycles
3) Any immediate data-transfer concerns for the listed processors (flag per-row in the attached CSV)

Karthik and Lauren are looped in for legal/procurement alignment. If you'd prefer, we can set a short 30-minute joint call this week to walk the list.

Thanks —
Sergio
Head of Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: subprocessor_inventory_20261112.csv

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acmecloud.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: vendor-security@acmecloud.com
Date: 2026-11-12T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Vendor notification: upcoming subprocessor additions and proposed objection cadence

Sergio — thanks for the heads-up and for the inventory. A couple of quick clarifying points from the security and legal side:

- Can you confirm which of the three new processors will receive raw customer identifiers vs. pseudonymized aggregates? We marked the CSV with a few questions.
- For EU-origin data, we require either SCCs in place or a documented transfer risk assessment. Do you have a copy of your most recent transfer assessment?
- We typically run a 45-day procurement review for new subprocessors that touch PII; would Redwood consider a 45-day objection window instead of 30?

I've attached our vendor-security-questionnaire — please have your team answer the data-flow items (pages 4–6) and return it. Procurement will need that to sign off.

We can do DocuSign; procurement prefers DocuSign envelopes with a single signatory from each party. If you send an envelope link, I can route it internally.

—Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Compliance, AcmeCloud

Attachments: vendor-security-questionnaire.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acmecloud.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-13T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Vendor notification: upcoming subprocessor additions and proposed objection cadence

Liam — thanks for the quick reply and the questionnaire. Sergio: looping in legal formally here.

High-level position from Redwood Legal: we can accommodate a 45-day procurement window as a one-time concession for this onboarding batch given enterprise procurement timelines, with the following caveats reflected in a short amendment:
- The notification period will be 30 days as standard; the "objection window" for procurement escalation may be extended to 45 days for certain enterprise accounts (explicitly listed in the amendment)
- If an objection is raised, both parties commit to a joint risk-call within 7 business days and to share technical artifacts (SCC mapping, transfer risk assessment) within 5 business days of the call
- During active objection resolution, we will not activate the processor for your account until both sides agree or compensating controls are documented in writing

I prepared a redline to the DPA that captures the above and clarifies the e-sign flow. Please review the attached (DPA_redline_karthik_20261113.pdf). Sergio — if Acme agrees to the 45-day procurement exception for this cohort, we will proceed with DocuSign execution per Lauren's routing instructions.

If Acme prefers AdobeSign, please confirm — our standard envelope supports either.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA_redline_karthik_20261113.pdf

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acmecloud.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-14T14:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Vendor notification: upcoming subprocessor additions and proposed objection cadence

Hi all — procurement here.

We will route the DPA amendment via DocuSign. Please confirm the signatory name and title on your side for the envelope (so we can pre-fill fields). Our PO will be attached to the envelope at signing.

Requested flow:
1) Redwood sends DocuSign envelope to Acme (single signatory)
2) Acme signs and returns — procurement countersigns immediately after
3) Executed PDF and audit trail stored in the deal folder (Drive link below)

I've attached our PO for reference. If Acme needs AdobeSign instead, tell us now so we change the envelope provider.

PO attached: PO_45872.pdf

Thanks, Lauren
Director, Strategic Procurement
Redwood Inference

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acmecloud.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-15T16:02:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Vendor notification: upcoming subprocessor additions and proposed objection cadence

Thanks everyone — we reviewed the redline with procurement and security. AcmeCloud can accept the 45-day procurement exception for this batch. We completed the vendor questionnaire and attached our subprocessor flags. No immediate objections on the three processors identified; security has requested SCCs and the transfer assessment — please attach those to the signed amendment.

DocuSign: envelope completed (https://app.docusign.com/envelope/status/ABCD-1234-ENVELOPE). Audit trail shows single signatory from AcmeCloud and countersign from Redwood procurement. Executed PDF is in the deal folder.

Next steps:
- Redwood: upload SCC mapping + transfer assessment to the Drive folder and link in the ticket
- AcmeCloud: will raise a formal objection within the 45-day window if any downstream issue appears; otherwise we consider the batch cleared for activation after the window closes

Regards,
Liam O'Connor
Head of Compliance, AcmeCloud

Attachments: acme_subprocessors_101.pdf
